analysis.title: October's ghost (Interest Rates Daily, 16 November 2026)
key_insights: USD rates curve moves reflect fears the Fed can fall behind the curve. Last week's bear steepening suggests short-term forces have overtaken the medium-term dovish forces (AI oversight concerns, data centre construction constraints).

Robust demand, persistent supply disruptions (imports and energy) and a tight labour market point to a stronger expansionary impulse than expected, raising the risk the Fed lags in its policy response.
Fed Governor Waller advocated 50bp insurance hikes if inflation persists. Most FOMC members prefer faster tightening starting in January rather than an outsized December move.

The six-week rally has room to unwind further. Only genuine progress in the Middle East or tightening financial conditions would impede further terminal rate increases and depricing of subsequent implied cuts.
Data suggest the Fed should have hiked in October. This is expected to reverberate to the long end through a higher Fed trajectory expectation and term premium.

EUR curves are exposed to the same steepening pressure with a beta of roughly 0.5. A more proactive ECB, 2027 GDP growth back to trend and close to no implied easing on the curve limit term premium creation.
Higher capex in defence, infrastructure and energy after prolonged underinvestment is a shared theme in the euro area, with a stronger fiscal headwind than in the US.
A Fed hike in December is widely expected. CACIB expects more scepticism from Fed members this week, enough to put the 50bp debate to rest.
A 25bp ECB hike in December is also a given, though slightly less so than the Fed hike. ECB leadership vacancies and Lagarde succession planning should dominate European headlines.
Week ahead: US retail sales Tuesday (modest growth expected outside autos and gas), Fed October minutes and ECB Financial Stability Review Wednesday, new European Commission forecasts Tuesday.
